title: Simple Past, Present and Future
keyIdea: The simple tenses tell when something happens, using one verb or will plus one verb. The simple past is for something that is over: I walked, she went. The simple present is for habits and facts that happen again and again: I walk, she walks; with he, she, it or one person the verb adds s, es after ch, sh, s, x or z (he watches), and a consonant then y becomes ies (it flies). The simple future is will followed by the plain verb with no ending: I will walk, she will walk, never she will walks or will walked. Time clues such as yesterday, every Saturday and tomorrow tell you which form to use, and one piece of writing keeps to one time unless the time really changes.
familyTip: Play yesterday, every day, tomorrow. Pick an action such as feed the cat. Your child says it three ways, one for each clue: yesterday I fed the cat, every day I feed the cat, tomorrow I will feed the cat. Then swap the person to she and listen for the s in she feeds.

visual.caption: Past, present or future? Drag each verb, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort time clues, add s, es or ies, drop will + verb into a gap, fill a tense table, fix a plan that slips, rebuild one sentence.

kid: A verb can tell you when. Past means it is over. Present means it happens again and again. Future means it has not happened yet.
Look for a time clue. Yesterday and last night point to the past. Every day and usually point to the present. Tomorrow and next week point to the future.

In the present, I, you, we and they use the plain verb: we play. He, she and it add an s: she plays. Some words add es: he watches. If a word ends in a consonant and y, the y turns into ies: it flies.
For the future, put will in front of the plain verb. I will swim. She will swim. Never add s or ed after will. Keep one story in one time.
adult: Ages 8 to 9. The US Common Core asks Grade 3 pupils to form and use the simple verb tenses. Its own example is I walked; I walk; I will walk (L.3.1e). In England, pupils must use present and past tense correctly and consistently from Year 2. The English glossary calls will a modal verb, not a future tense. This lesson still uses the label future for will plus a verb, as US books do.

Three forms do the work. The simple past is one verb, with -ed or an odd form: walked, went, tried. The simple present is the plain verb. Only he, she, it or one thing adds an ending: s (walks), es after ch, sh, s, x or z (watches), or ies for a consonant plus y (carries). A vowel plus y just adds s (plays). The simple future is will plus the plain verb, and it never changes for the person: she will walk. The simple present is mostly for habits and facts. Something happening right now usually takes the -ing form (I am walking), so the lab pairs the present with clues like every day and usually.

Common mistakes: adding s or ed after will (she will goes, they will went); dropping the s for he or she (the baby cry); spelling slips such as carrys and searchs; reading the present as right now only, so every Monday goes in the wrong box; and tense drift. In Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk, one verb slips out of the time the rest of the piece uses.

In the lab your child sorts nine time clues and adds the right ending to eight present verbs. They drag will plus the plain verb into four gaps and fill a tense table for walk, go and try. Then they fix the two verbs that slip in a future plan, and rebuild I walk to school for three times.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is in the simple future?
choices: Tomorrow I will walk to school.
Tomorrow I will walked to school.
practice.hint: The future uses will. What form of the verb comes after will?
practice.explain: The future is will plus the plain verb: I will walk. walked is the past, and will walked mixes the two.

practice.prompt: A diary has {n} verbs. {k} of them are in the past. The rest are in the present. How many are in the present?
practice.hint: Take the past verbs away from all the verbs.

practice.prompt: Every day my little brother ___ his toys. (carry)
practice.hint: My brother is one person. carry ends in a consonant and y.
practice.explain: For he, she or one person, a consonant then y changes to ies: carries. carrys is a spelling slip, and carry has no ending.

practice.prompt: Mia writes {a} future sentences on Monday and {b} on Tuesday. Each one uses will once. How many times does she write will?
practice.hint: One will in each sentence. Add the two days.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} sentences, so will appears {=a+b} times, each one followed by a plain verb.

practice.prompt: Find the verb that slips: "Yesterday she walks to the shop and bought milk."
practice.hint: Yesterday and bought both point to the past. Which verb does not match?
practice.explain: walks is present, but the rest is past. Fix it to walked: Yesterday she walked to the shop and bought milk.

pool.prompt: Pick the simple future: "Next week we ___ to the beach."
pool.hint: After will, the verb has no ending and is not a past form.
pool.explain: will plus the plain verb: we will go. went is a past form and goes has an s, so neither fits after will.

pool.prompt: Which time clue goes with the simple present?
pool.hint: The simple present is for things that happen again and again.
pool.explain: every Saturday is a habit, so it takes the present: every Saturday I swim. last night is past and next year is future.

pool.hint: fetch ends in ch. Every morning is a habit.
pool.explain: After ch, add es: fetches. You can hear the extra beat. fetched is the past, which does not match every morning.

pool.prompt: Change "I play football" to the past.
pool.hint: The past is over. Which form has -ed?
pool.explain: The simple past of play is played: I played football. will play is future, and plays is only for he, she or it.

pool.prompt: Which sentence keeps to one time?
choices: Tomorrow we will bake a cake and Dad will help.
Tomorrow we will bake a cake and Dad helped.
Tomorrow we bake a cake and Dad will helped.
pool.hint: Tomorrow is the future. Both verbs need will plus the plain verb.
pool.explain: Both verbs are in the future: will bake, will help. helped slips into the past, and will helped breaks the will rule.

pool.prompt: A tense table has {v} verbs, and each verb needs a past, a present and a future form. How many boxes are there?
Tonight the moon ___ in the sky. (shine) Which form shows the future?
pool.hint: The future uses will in front of the plain verb.
pool.explain: will shine is the future. shines is present and shone is past.

pool.prompt: A story has {n} verbs. {k} slip out of the past into the present. How many verbs are already right?
pool.hint: Take the slips away from all the verbs.
pool.explain: {n} − {k} = {=n-k} verbs keep to the past. The {k} slips need changing back.

pool.prompt: Every afternoon the cat ___ in the sun. (lie) Pick the present.
pool.hint: The cat is one animal. Every afternoon is a habit.
pool.explain: For he, she, it or one thing, the present adds s: the cat lies. will lies is wrong because nothing takes s after will.

pool.prompt: Which word shows that a sentence is in the future?
pool.hint: Which word goes in front of the plain verb to show it has not happened yet?
pool.explain: will marks the simple future: I will walk. was is past and usually is a present time clue.
